# Frozen goal-calibration corpus for tests/goal_model_minilm.rs. Do not edit
# casually: changing a line changes the recorded calibration numbers.
# Format: "@goal <id> <goal text>" then one source per line:
#   <R|I>|<kind>|<source id>|<title>|<text>
# R relevant, I irrelevant. kinds: lexical (relevant, shares goal words),
# paraphrase (relevant, few goal words), nearmiss (irrelevant, shares goal
# words), unrelated (irrelevant, different topic).

@goal g01 how ocean tides are caused by the moon
R|lexical|g01-a|Tides explained|Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the moon, which draws the water on the near side of the earth into a bulge.
R|lexical|g01-b|Why the moon moves the ocean|The moon causes two tides a day because its gravity stretches the ocean toward it and, less obviously, away from it.
R|paraphrase|g01-c|Spring and neap cycles|Coastal water rises and falls twice daily as our satellite tugs on the seas; when sun and satellite line up the swings grow largest.
R|paraphrase|g01-d|Lunar gravity and the shore|Harbour depth changes through the day because the natural satellite's attraction deforms the planet's liquid surface.
I|nearmiss|g01-e|Moon landing anniversary|The moon landing was watched by millions; astronauts collected rock samples and planted a flag near the ocean of storms crater.
I|nearmiss|g01-f|Ocean cleanup report|Plastic pollution in the ocean is caused by fishing nets and packaging, and new boats are being built to remove it.
I|unrelated|g01-g|Sourdough starter guide|Feed your starter flour and water every day and keep it somewhere warm until it doubles in size.

@goal g02 fix a memory leak in a Rust program
R|lexical|g02-a|Finding leaks in Rust|To fix a memory leak in a Rust program, check for reference cycles with Rc and RefCell and break them using Weak pointers.
R|lexical|g02-b|Rust leak debugging|A growing Rust program usually leaks memory through forgotten channels or cached values that are never removed from a map.
R|paraphrase|g02-c|Heap profiling walkthrough|Run the binary under heaptrack and compare allocation snapshots to see which function keeps allocating without ever freeing.
R|paraphrase|g02-d|Cycles with Arc|Two structs holding strong Arc handles to each other will never be dropped, so the allocation lives until the process exits.
I|nearmiss|g02-e|Rust game review|Rust the survival game has a memory of its own: players leak into each other's bases and a program of events fixes the map.
I|nearmiss|g02-f|Rust removal on cars|Preventing rust on a car body means fixing chips quickly; a leak in the door seal lets moisture sit in the metal.
I|unrelated|g02-g|Marathon pacing|Start the first miles slowly, take water every five kilometres and save energy for the final stretch.

R|lexical|g03-b|Cost of ownership|Compared with petrol cars, electric cars have fewer moving parts, so servicing costs less over ten years.
R|paraphrase|g03-c|Charging at home|Plugging in overnight on a cheap tariff can cost a third of what the same distance costs at the fuel pump.
R|paraphrase|g03-d|Battery vehicles and the wallet|Owners of battery vehicles save on maintenance and fuel, though depreciation and a pricey purchase can eat into the gain.

I|unrelated|g03-g|Gardening in autumn|Plant tulip bulbs before the first frost and mulch the beds to protect them over winter.

R|lexical|g06-b|Learn chess openings|Beginners learn the opening basics by moving centre pawns first and bringing knights out before bishops.

R|paraphrase|g06-d|Early game habits|Avoid moving the same piece twice or launching an early queen raid; instead build a sound structure quickly.

@goal g07 how photosynthesis converts sunlight into energy in plants
R|lexical|g07-a|Photosynthesis basics|Photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy in plants, using chlorophyll to turn water and carbon dioxide into sugar.
R|lexical|g07-b|How plants make energy|In plants, sunlight is converted into energy during photosynthesis: light reactions capture photons, then the Calvin cycle builds glucose.
R|paraphrase|g07-c|Leaves as factories|Green pigment in foliage absorbs rays and drives the production of carbohydrates from air and water, releasing oxygen as waste.
R|paraphrase|g07-d|Chloroplast chemistry|Inside tiny organelles, captured light splits water molecules and powers the assembly of food molecules for the organism.
I|nearmiss|g07-e|Solar panel installation|Sunlight is converted into electricity by panels on your roof; installers say energy bills fall, and plants nearby may shade them.
I|nearmiss|g07-f|Power plants and energy|Coal power plants convert fuel into energy, and sunlight rarely figures in how they work.
I|unrelated|g07-g|Jazz piano voicings|Rootless voicings leave the bass to another player and stack extensions above the guide tones.
